met_analysis:
The Low Pressure area over Western parts of Gangetic West Bengal & neighbourhood lies over Western parts of Gangetic West Bengal & adjoining north Jharkhand at 0530 hrs IST of today, 18th July, 2026. The associated cyclonic circulation extends upto 5.8 km above mean sea level tilting southwestwards with height. It is very likely to weaken gradually during next 24 hrs.
The Monsoon trough at mean sea level now passes through Amritsar, Karnal, Bareilly, Lucknow, Patna, centre of Low Pressure area over Western parts of Gangetic West Bengal & adjoining north Jharkhand, Diamond harbour and thence southeastwards towards Northeast Bay of Bengal and extends upto 0.9 km above mean sea level.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over north Haryana & neighbourhoodupto 1.5 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over east Uttar Pradesh persists now seen between 1.5 & 3.1 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over southwest Rajasthan & neighbourhood at 3.1 km above mean sea level persists.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over Gulf of Mannar adjoining south Tamil Nadu at 5.8 km above mean sea level.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over north Kerala & neighbourhood at 5.8 km above mean sea level.
The trough from North Lakshadweep area to southwest Bay of Bengal across north Kerala, South Interior Karnataka and north Tamilnadu at 7.6 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Northeast Assam & neighbourhood extending upto 1.5 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
The Western Disturbance as cyclonic circulation over north Pakistan & neighbourhood at 5.8 km above mean sea level has become less marked, however the trough aloft in upper level westerlies with its axis at 7.6 km above mean sea level now runs roughly along Long. 70°E to the north of Lat. 30°N.
